::: {.key-question}
What external factors influence health and wellbeing for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people and families in the NEPHU catchment, including in supporting children and strong families?
:::

## Internet Use for Connection and Everyday Life

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 17](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/access-information/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have access to information and services enabling participation in informed decision-making regarding their own lives**

Target: By 2026, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have equal levels of digital inclusion.
:::

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Personal use of the internet in previous three months
# Data from ABS Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
digital_status <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Digital_Status.csv")

# Data wrangling
digital_status <- digital_status %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(has_personally_used_the_internet_in_the_last_3_months_n:has_not_personally_used_the_internet_in_the_last_3_months_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(used_n    = has_personally_used_the_internet_in_the_last_3_months_n,
                notused_n = has_not_personally_used_the_internet_in_the_last_3_months_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(used_n:notused_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("used"),
                starts_with("notused"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "used"     = "Yes",
                                              "notused"  = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reasons for using the internet
# Data from ABS Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
digital_reason <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Digital_Reason.csv")

# Data wrangling
digital_reason <- digital_reason %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = total_n - not_applicable_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(social_n     = social_networking_n,
                shopping_n   = purchasing_or_ordering_goods_or_services_online_n,
                banking_n    = paying_bills_or_banking_online_n,
                health_n     = health_services_n,
                work_n       = work_purposes_n,
                education_n  = formal_educational_activities_n,
                government_n = accessing_government_services_or_information_about_government_services_n,
                volunteer_n  = volunteering_or_participating_in_community_groups_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(social_n:other_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("social"),
                starts_with("shopping"),
                starts_with("banking"),
                starts_with("entertainment"),
                starts_with("health"),
                starts_with("work"),
                starts_with("education"),
                starts_with("government"),
                starts_with("volunteer"),
                starts_with("other"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "social"        = "Social media",
                                              "shopping"      = "Online shopping",
                                              "banking"       = "Online banking",
                                              "entertainment" = "Entertainment",
                                              "health"        = "Health services",
                                              "work"          = "Work",
                                              "education"     = "Education",
                                              "government"    = "Government services",
                                              "volunteer"     = "Volunteering",
                                              "other"         = "Other reasons",
                                              "answered"      = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Social media",
                                           "Online shopping",
                                           "Online banking",
                                           "Entertainment",
                                           "Health services",
                                           "Work",
                                           "Education",
                                           "Government services",
                                           "Volunteering",
                                           "Other reasons",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 96% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had used the internet during the three months prior to the survey. This equates to approximately 35,800 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people in Greater Melbourne.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to have used the internet than females (98% vs. 93%).

- The most common reasons for accessing the internet were entertainment (84%, approximately 28,500 people), social media (80%, approximately 27,200 people), and online shopping (67%, approximately 22,900 people).

- Males were more likely to access the internet than females for social media (82% vs. 77%), health services (38% vs. 30%), and work (55% vs. 44%) while females were more likely to access the internet for education (41% vs. 31%) and volunteering (16% vs. 7.8%).

- Comparable non-Indigenous data on internet usage are not available, and this is [acknowledged as a limitation](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/access-information/) of Closing the Gap Target 17.

- Further historical and ongoing target context can be found on the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/access-information/).

::: {.callout-tip title="Survey questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.
  - Have you personally used the internet in the last three months? This could have been through devices such as mobile phones, smart watches, laptops, computers, tablets, game consoles, or internet enabled televisions.
    - `r note_response_binary`
  - In the last three months, did you use the internet for any of these reasons? (Select all that apply)
    - Social networking (e.g. Facebook, Twitter, Skype)
    - Purchasing or ordering goods or services online (e.g. travel, tickets, accommodation, computer software, clothes, food, movies, music, books)
    - Paying bills or banking online
    - Entertainment (e.g. playing or downloading games, music, movies, television)
    - Health services (e.g. Telehealth, making medical appointments)
    - None of the above
  - In the last three months, did you use the internet for any of these reasons? (Select all that apply)
    - Work purposes
    - Formal education activities
    - Accessing government services or information about government services (e.g. tax, benefits payments, licences)
    - Volunteering or participating in community groups
    - None of the above

:::

```{r}
#
figtab_table_count  <- figtab_table_count + 1
figtab_table_title  <- paste0("Table", " ", figtab_report_section, "-", figtab_table_count)
figtab_table_number <- paste0("Table_", figtab_csv_section, "_", sprintf("%.02d", figtab_table_count))
```

#### `r figtab_table_title`

::: {.fig-tab-title}
**`r figtab_table_title`:** Personal use of the internet during the three months prior to the survey for survey respondents who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, Greater Melbourne, by sex, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
#
table <- digital_status %>% 
  f_preptable_grouped_sex(variable_name = "internet_accessed")

if (!file.exists(paste0(here::here(), "/data/", figtab_table_number, ".csv"))) {
  
  write.csv(table, paste0(here::here(), "/data/", figtab_table_number, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
}

table %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(prop_male   = sprintf("%.1f", prop_male),
                prop_female = sprintf("%.1f", prop_female),
                prop_total  = sprintf("%.1f", prop_total)) %>%
  #
  f_table_grouped_sex(n_variable  = "estimate",
                      column_name = "Used internet during<br>previous three months")
```

#### `r figtab_figure_title`

::: {.fig-tab-title}
**`r figtab_figure_title`:** Reasons for accessing the internet during the three months prior to the survey for survey respondents who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, Greater Melbourne, by sex, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
#
factor_levels <- stringr::str_wrap(levels(digital_reason$answer), width = 15)

figure_number <- digital_reason %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & answer != "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 15), levels = factor_levels)) %>% 
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = n,
                    x_angle    = 90)

figure_percent <- digital_reason %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & answer != "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 15), levels = factor_levels)) %>% 
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = prop,
                    x_angle    = 90)

f_bar_grouped_combine(figure_number, figure_percent, legend_offset = -0.35)
```
